results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 49 outline summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph (p01-p49), in spec order; the summaries that omit a paragraph's labeled reading (p24, p26, p34, p36) do so because that reading sits in the paragraph's own INFERENCE callout, as the spec's evidence declares.

The Business: Where the Money Comes From ¶2: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p09's controlling idea joins the GMV-linked revenue mix with the plan mix and the two-supplier dependence as one reading (a payments-and-platform business).
Inventory States, Briefly ¶1: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p30's controlling idea joins the stock states with the missing B2B allocation and ATP and the resulting W1 decision.
The Ecosystem: Apps, Scopes, Webhooks and Versions ¶2: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p32's controlling idea declares the App Store as both a business and a governance regime.
The Ecosystem: Apps, Scopes, Webhooks and Versions ¶4: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p34's controlling idea joins dated API versions and per-app rate limits.
Peak Days With Definitions ¶2: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p36's controlling idea joins the 2023/2025 preparation with the 2018 checkout queue.
AI and the Agent Surface: Rebuilt Within a Year ¶3: marked two_ideas by the outliner, but p39's controlling idea joins the geography with the argument for adapters.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: method to S6; business to S1; monolith to S2; pods to S3; storefront, checkout, payments, inventory and ecosystem/peak/ai to S1/S4; transfers to S5; evidence to S6; conclusion to the thesis and so_what.

All four tables are introduced and read (business table by p08/p09 and the inference callout; checkout timeline by p25/p26 and callout; BFCM table by p35's caveats and the ratio callout; transfers table by p40 and p41). Figures 1-4 follow the text they picture with explanatory captions. Quotations carry date and source; the six INFERENCE callouts are labeled as the author's reasoning.

results.quote: A **monolith** is one deployable application that holds all of the shop's logic
results.finding: The spec declares a cause_effect transition carrying over 'one single-branch platform serving millions of shops' and introducing 'how Shopify organized the codebase behind it'. The section opens with a bare definition; nothing links the 10-K's single-branch, multi-tenant platform to the codebase question, so the declared cause-effect is not expressed.

results.quote: Stock can be physically present but unavailable to sell because it is damaged, reserved or already promised to another order
results.finding: The spec declares a sequence transition carrying over 'checkout and payment' and introducing 'the stock the order draws on'. The section opens on a general definition of unavailable stock with no reference to the checkout and payment just covered; both flow readers also noted the missing lead-in.

All other declared transition_in boundaries are expressed: intro p02-p05 (elaboration, place label, claim label, sequence); method, business, storefront, checkout, payments, ecosystem and ai section openings follow the roadmap's announced sequence; peak ('Rate limits bind hardest at peak'), pods ('One codebase is not one database'), transfers and evidence; paragraph transitions in monolith (time, additional_support, emphasis 'And the sentence that matters most', contrast 'The one documented case'), pods, storefront, checkout ('What replaced the freedom'), payments, ecosystem, peak, ai, transfers ('Only Shopify needs the rest'), conclusion labels (Established / Depends on context / The author's synthesis), 'These points become questions', and the contrast hand-off to case-amazon ('Amazon, the next case, is a different kind of company').

Organising principle: both flow readers describe money first, then architecture (code, then data isolation), then the parts of the order, the contract, peak and agents, then the synthesis, which agrees with the declared grouping with large_to_small and chronological sub-patterns; both say the large-scale order works. Points both readers raised about terms on audience.already_knows (the Forked Platform, WMS, Group, Waypoint references) are not counted as failures.

Every does_not_know term is given before or where it is used: GMV, merchant, MRR, Payments penetration (share of GMV), subscription and merchant solutions; multi-tenant, single branch, monolith, modular monolith, component (labeled domain groupings), Packwerk, shard, sharding key, pod, Storefront Renderer; theme, Liquid, headless, Hydrogen, Oxygen, Storefront API, Lighthouse, checkout extensibility, Functions, WebAssembly, Shop Pay, PCI DSS, payment orchestration; scope, OAuth, HMAC, rate limits, version window; BFCM, CDN, edge vs app-server (via the ratio callout); MCP, UCP, Catalog, agent profile, trust tiers, Sidekick. Terms flow readers flagged (WMS, Forked Platform, Group, Growing stage) are on already_knows.
The introduction opens on the reader's question (which work the platform takes on), places the case in the order's journey, states the claim and gives a roadmap; no generic or throat-clearing opener.
The conclusion answers the opening question, separates established, context-dependent and authorial points, ends in questions and a contrast hand-off; no mere restatement or new-topic ending.

p44 synthesizes (machinery is the landlord's, the joins are the merchant's) and the so-what is stated: pin, reconcile, track sunsets, budget against the landlord's cadence, keep custom behavior out of checkout, ask vendors for the unit of isolation (author's synthesis and questions 1-8).
'Which work does the platform take on, and which is the merchant's?' repeats the opening question of Introduction ¶1 and answers it with the landlord image the introduction set up.

Reader explains the deleted subscription after 8 consecutive failures over 4 hours (outage longer than the retry window, so nothing logged), unguaranteed and unordered delivery, and names subscription checks, reconciliation (W5), idempotent handling by webhook id and pinned API versions; substantially matches expected (support end/owner only implied).

Reader's adopt list (reconciled at-least-once webhooks, pinned versions as maintenance budget, no withdrawable checkout customization, lowest bounded place, rate-limit budget and one writer, scaled-down load tests on connectors/ERP/WMS with caches bypassed, isolation question) and do-not-copy list (pods, Ghostferry moves, edge rendering, observability platform, March readiness program) with the landlord-cadence reason substantially match expected; it omits shadow comparison before cutover and files boundary gates under in-house code only, consistent with the chapter.

Reader corrects the slogan with the 2019 labeling, the 2020 state (37 components, each depending on over half), Packwerk kept only as a base-layer gate with privacy checks removed, the 2024 admission, ownership as what paid off, and the Storefront Renderer carved for speed behind a verifier; matches expected.

The intro reader predicts the question, the claim, the section order (evidence note, business, monolith and isolation, storefront/checkout/payment/inventory, app contract, peak, agents, transfers, evidence stops), the dated evidence kinds (FY2025 filing and Q3 2026; 2018-2024 posts, docs, changelog, treated as dated) and the three failure patterns; substantially matches expected.
